title: Small protein, big effects: ENOD93 alters mitochondrial ATP production to favor nitrogen assimilation in plants
content: Mitochondria are referred to as the powerhouse of the cell, and in plants, they generate the majority of ATP needed to energize various cytosolic processes. Oxidative phosphorylation of ADP to ATP occurs when a proton motive force generated across the mitochondrial inner membrane by electron transfer through a series of respiratory chain complexes fuels the ATP synthase complex. Respiratory complex IV catalyzes the terminal electron transfer from cytochrome c to molecular oxygen, reducing it to water, and contributes to the proton gradient by pumping protons across the inner membrane. In yeast, a protein called Rcf2 supports the proton motive force generation by complex IV (Strogolova et al. 2019). However, its counterpart in plants was so far unknown.
